business_scope.primary_industry_name: Virtual Expense Card Issuing and Spend Management Controls

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Civil Law (French-model codified statutes) with Islamic Sharia as a supplementary source of legislation under Article 2 of the Egyptian Constitution
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Unified Agreement for the Investment of Arab Capital in the Arab States (1980, as amended)
Agadir Agreement for the Establishment of a Free Trade Zone among Egypt, Jordan, Morocco, and Tunisia (2004)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: AML Law No. 80 of 2002 concerning Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and applicable Central Bank of Egypt circulars; Executive Regulations of the AML Law issued under Ministry of Justice Decree No. 3012 of 2002, as amended; Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020; Payments and Payment Services Regulation Law No. 18 of 2019; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, requiring disclosure of beneficial ownership data to the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) at incorporation; UBO registers maintained by GAFI and the Egyptian Money Laundering Combating and Terrorist Financing Unit (EMLCU) are government-access only and subject to FATF-directed record-retention obligations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Notary Public and corporate registry of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (issued by the competent authority in the country of origin) OR Consular Legalization through the Egyptian Embassy or Consulate in the issuing country; followed by certified Arabic translation submitted to GAFI

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Commercial Registry Extract of the parent shareholder entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official companies registrar of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization at the Egyptian diplomatic mission in the issuing country, with certified Arabic translation where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorizing incorporation of the Egyptian LLC and appointing the local manager, UBO representatives, and compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the parent shareholder entity assembled before a Notary Public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization at the Egyptian diplomatic mission in the issuing country, with certified Arabic translation where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of the passports of all ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs), directors, and officers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport-issuing authority, Notary Public, or sworn translator in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization at the Egyptian diplomatic mission in the issuing country; bilingual certified translation to accompany the original

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney in favor of the Egyptian incorporating attorney or the designated local manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization at the Egyptian diplomatic mission in the issuing country, with certified Arabic translation submitted to GAFI and the Commercial Registry

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the EMLCU domestic terrorist financing circular list; Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is required for all Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) under FATF Recommendation 12, including origin of wealth and source of funds verification; any suspicious transaction or attempted relationship must be reported to the EMLCU within 24 hours pursuant to AML Law No. 80 of 2002; nominee or low-transparency staggered ownership structures are prohibited where the underlying UBO cannot be identified at or above the 25% threshold.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols_sh: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic screening per AML Law 80/2002 and FATF standards; 24-hour STR window and EDD for PEPs.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI e-Registration and Company Incorporation Portal (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones), administered pursuant to Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and Companies Law No. 159 of 1981
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name must be registered in Arabic script and must include the legal-form suffix 'شركة ذات مسؤولية محدودة' (Limited Liability Company); a Latin/English transliteration may be additionally recorded for banking, card-network, and trademark purposes, but the Arabic version is the authoritative registered name; names comprising more than four words or containing acronyms without a clear Arabic meaning are generally rejected; any reference to 'Bank', 'Finance', 'Payments', 'Egyptian', 'Arab Republic of Egypt', or state-entity terminology requires prior regulatory clearance from the competent authority, including the Central Bank of Egypt for payment-related terms.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: شركة مصر / Egyptian state-associated wording implying government ownership or sponsorship
جهة سيادية / sovereign, presidential, military, or state-authority connotations
Payments / Payment Systems or card-network terms where a CBE license is not yet granted
Mastercard, Visa, or other registered card-network brand marks without authorized licensor consent
Words contrary to public order, morality, or misleading the public as to nationality, activity, or capital
Any name identical or confusingly similar to an existing name in the GAFI Commercial Registry
Unlicensed 'Islamic' finance or investment-fund terminology requiring the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A written administrative appeal may be filed with the GAFI Name Clearance Committee within 30 days of a formal rejection, attaching the refusal notice, a sworn Arabic translation of the proposed name, and not less than two alternative names; GAFI must issue a reasoned decision within 15 business days; if the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may initiate an annulment action before the First Instance Administrative Court of the State Council within 60 days of notification, per the State Council Law No. 47 of 1972 read with Law No. 119 of 2008; each re-filing of a rejected name requires payment of the applicable GAFI service fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is acceptable solely as a limited administrative correspondence address, but is legally insufficient as the sole premises for this business scope; the Central Bank of Egypt requires licensed electronic-payment and card-issuing entities to maintain a physical place of business in Egypt, with a permanently available compliance officer, board meeting facilities, protected record storage, and auditable access to core payment systems; GAFI also mandates a substantive local registered office address for the LLC at incorporation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (estimated at >85% probability) for a 'High_Risk_Special_License' virtual card issuer, including unannounced on-site inspections by the Central Bank of Egypt supervision teams, EMLCU thematic AML/CFT visits, and GAFI compliance verification during the first operational year.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018 and its Executive Regulations; Articles 24-26 (formation and memorandum of association of limited liability companies), Article 76 (appointment and powers of managers); Commercial Registry Rules under Presidential Decree No. 491 of 1954.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Registration and Commercial Registry Directorate
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Establishment Contract (Memorandum of Association) together with the annexed Articles of Association, submitted through GAFI's Integrated Investment Window
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Egyptian Companies Law does not impose a statutory minimum paid-up capital at formation; the authorized capital must be stated in the Articles of Association. For the licensed corporate virtual-card issuer activity, Central Bank of Egypt payment-service licensing instructions require a committed paid-up capital of at least EGP 25,000,000 deposited in a blocked account at a licensed Egyptian bank and maintained until the operating license is granted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF MANAGERS OF EG_LLC. The undersigned, comprising the founders' designated officers, acting unanimously pursuant to the Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and the Articles of Association, hereby resolve: (1) each subscriber listed on the annexed subscription schedule is allotted shares in the amounts opposite their name, fully paid-up by deposit of EGP [capital] to the company account; (2) the registered office is fixed at 15 Sheikh Reyhan Street, Cairo, Egypt; the managers are authorized to execute lease, utilities, and procurement agreements; and (3) [Name], [Name], and [Name] are appointed as Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Company Secretary, respectively, with statutory powers to conduct all filings and banking operations. Effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Pre-Incorporation Legal Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop / GAFI Name Reservation Online Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed company names in Arabic and English, together with a short statement of objectives. Pay the name reservation fee, obtain the name reservation certificate, and verify that the intended licensed activity is described in the business-object clause. Prepare draft establishment contract and articles of association using GAFI template forms.
required_dossiers: Passport copies or national ID copies of all intended shareholders
Power of attorney if a corporate subscriber acts through a representative
Statement of business scope and proposed objectives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or impermissible wording, file an amended name-reservation request with alternative names; objections to refusal may be lodged with the GAFI Name Committee within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Authentication of Establishment Contract and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Incorporation Documentation Unit and Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Shareholders or their duly authorized representatives must appear before the GAFI notifications and notarization unit to sign the Establishment Contract and Articles of Association. Foreign corporate shareholders must provide apostilled or certified board resolutions and powers of attorney. The notary authenticates signatures and seals the founding documents.
required_dossiers: Draft Establishment Contract and Articles of Association
Valid passports or national IDs of individual shareholders
Apostilled/certified corporate documents and board authorization for corporate shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or GAFI reviewer issues a correction notice, cure the identified deficiency by filing the corrected original or notarized document within 15 days; no new filing fee is assessed for the first resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription Account and Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in Egypt supervised by the Central Bank of Egypt
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional bank account in the company name using the name reservation certificate and draft establishment contract. Deposit the declared paid-up capital or obtain a bankers' letter confirming the blocked licensed-activity capital. The bank issues a capital deposit certificate for inclusion in the GAFI filing package.
required_dossiers: Beneficial ownership declaration and source-of-funds statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the capital deposit, supplement the file with enhanced AML/KYC declarations and updated beneficial-ownership documentation; resubmit through the bank's compliance committee for expedited review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Filing, Commercial Registration and Company Number Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized establishment contract, capital deposit certificate, registered-office lease or notarized usufruct agreement, copy of the bank account, first board resolution, auditor acceptance, and declaration of lawful physical premises. GAFI verifies, enters the company in the commercial registry, issues the company number, and issues the certificate of incorporation and commercial register extract.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease or legal-title document
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the file is rejected for address mismatch, lease defects, or incomplete declarations, submit corrected documents to the same file within 20 days; formal appeal against rejection may be filed with the GAFI Appeals Committee within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Identification and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority and National Social Insurance Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the company tax card, corporate taxpayer identification number, value-added tax registration where taxable, payroll withholding registration, and social insurance registration for all managers and employees. Complete the statistical statement and classify the company under the appropriate ISIC code.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and commercial register extract
Power of attorney for the registration representative
Lease agreement for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If issuance is delayed, escalate to the Tax Authority Service Center and National Social Insurance Authority complaints desk; request a provisional tax card while final validation is pending.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Corporate Governance Filings and Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Company File and Egyptian Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the final board resolution and register all officers and managers. Issue share certificates, prepare the shareholder register, board minutes book, and statutory corporate seals. Submit beneficial-ownership information to GAFI, and record any additions to the company's scope of activities.
required_dossiers: First board resolution and officers' appointment forms
Shareholders' register and share certificate templates
Specimen signature cards for registered managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI queries the beneficial-ownership statement or officer data, file a corrected return and provide notarized supporting declarations; late correction penalties may be waived if submitted proactively within 10 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Central Bank of Egypt - Payment Systems and Financial Technology Oversight Unit, with coordination by the Financial Regulatory Authority for non-banking financial services
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Payment System Service Provider License for Card Issuance and Spend-Management Controls, including the related digital financial services authorization

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency, Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B Regulatory-Range (Limited Development) - no full EIA report is required for office-only virtual-card operations; submit an environmental self-assessment and waste-management commitment form before commencement.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No liquid process discharge is permitted for the office-only use; sanitary effluent must comply with Law No. 4 of 1994 and EEAA Decree No. 53 of 1997. Standby generators, if installed, must meet Egyptian air-emission threshold values. Electronic waste from IT and card-production ancillary equipment must be handled through a licensed e-waste recycler. No VOC-emitting industrial equipment is authorized on site.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from the Egyptian Civil Defense Enterprise; structural load certificate confirming server-room and office-floor loading capacity; approved emergency evacuation plan; and workplace safety and occupational-health clearance from the Ministry of Manpower covering card-handling staff and IT operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – sole national tax administration for income tax, VAT, stamp duty and electronic fiscal systems. Official portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing/e-receipt fiscal clearance portal: https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg; unified digital tax card and Tax Register services operated under Law No. 206/2020.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must obtain a single unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) under Law No. 206/2020 before commencing activity. Procedure on the ETA portal: (i) upload the Arabic notarized memorandum of association and commercial registry extract; (ii) submit a board resolution appointing a resident tax representative and proof of registered office; (iii) simultaneously apply for VAT and e-invoicing profiles. The ETA issues an electronic tax card, normally within 30 days, which activates CIT, VAT, payroll tax and e-invoice obligations. Non-resident shareholders without an Egyptian presence must engage a licensed Egyptian tax agent to authenticate registration filings and receive ETA correspondence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (no pass-through eligibility). The Egyptian LLC is a juridical corporate tax resident subject to 22.5% CIT on worldwide income under Law No. 91/2005, as amended. Territorial_Scope: non-resident shareholders are taxed on Egyptian-source income only, through withholding taxes on dividends, interest and management fees. Unless the entity elects and obtains Special Economic Zone (e.g., SCZONE) or Free Zone status, it remains a standard-rate domestic taxpayer outside any customs- or tax-exempt zone.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not provide US-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections; entity classification is statutory. Available statutory elections are: (i) tax-group consolidation for subsidiaries under common ownership meeting the 95% threshold per Law No. 91/2005; (ii) election for an unincorporated joint venture to be taxed as a separate corporate person; (iii) Free Zone or Special Economic Zone license election under Investment Law No. 72/2017, which can confer customs/VAT exemptions on exported goods activity; (iv) VAT cash-basis accounting for eligible small taxpayers; and (v) ordinary CIT elections concerning depreciation rates and loss carryforward methodology.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016 and Executive Regulation No. 66/2017, administered by the Egyptian Tax Authority.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supplies for mandatory VAT registration; voluntary registration available from EGP 50,000; mandatory phase-in to the ETA e-invoicing ecosystem is turnover-based and now effectively captures all VAT-registered undertakings, including fintech payment issuers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The ETA operates a centralized real-time e-invoice and e-receipt fiscal clearance platform. VAT-registered taxpayers must generate invoices/receipts in the prescribed XML schema, transmit them via public or private APIs, and obtain the ETA digital signature, QR matrix and unique invoice ID prior to lawful issuance. Clearance is near-real-time and linked to customs release for imports; non-integrated sellers cannot issue deductible invoices, face transaction blocking and are excluded from claiming input VAT or zero-rated export treatment.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Article 20 of VAT Law No. 67/2016 zero-rates: (a) goods physically exported from Egypt within the statutory shipping window, evidenced by customs documents and foreign-currency remittance; and (b) services exported to a non-resident recipient where the benefit is enjoyed entirely outside Egypt and consideration is received in foreign currency remitted into Egypt. For the corporate virtual-card program, Mastercard/Visa network fees, switching, authorization and settlement services charged to non-resident program managers or foreign corporate cardholders are eligible for zero-rating; issuing and processing services supplied to Egyptian-resident clients are exempt financial services without input VAT recovery and must be strictly segregated from exported services in the VAT ledger.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (official export entry with HS codes and shipment particulars)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill proving physical departure from Egypt
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a licensed Egyptian bank evidencing foreign-currency receipt and repatriation
Zero-rated VAT tax invoice digitally cleared through the ETA e-invoicing platform
Underlying export service agreement or program management contract with the non-resident counterparty
Mastercard/Visa settlement and interchange reports evidencing offshore sourcing of the fees
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA may re-open export zero-rating claims retroactively for up to five tax years (six years where fraud is alleged). Any missing or falsified customs/remittance documentation automatically converts the supply to standard-rated 14% VAT; the ETA will assess the tax together with monthly late-payment penalties, impose a fidelity/evasion surcharge of up to 100% of the tax due, and may refer willful falsification for criminal prosecution. Improperly obtained VAT refunds are clawed back in full with statutory delay interest, and the exporter may be suspended from the ETA e-invoicing clearance system pending full rectification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), exercising exclusive FX administration under the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020 and the AML/CFT Law No. 80 of 2022; non-bank payment and card issuance supervision is shared with the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) pursuant to the Payment Systems Law No. 18 of 2019. All cross-border flows must be effected through CBE-licensed dealing banks and reported in the CBE international transactions reporting framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a unified, market-determined exchange rate for the Egyptian Pound (EGP) following the March 2024 liberalisation and has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations, so current-account payments, including profit remittances and trade settlements, are nominally free of quota or licensing restrictions. In practice, banks apply liquidity and prioritisation filters, and capital-account transactions, including equity injections and foreign-currency loans, require routing through licensed banks, GAFI registration and CBE capital-account reporting. Dividend remittances require an audited balance sheet letter or tax clearance certificate plus inclusion in the CBE/GAFI investor database; due to the High-Risk Special License classification, enhanced due diligence may extend remittance cycles.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: CBE instructions require export proceeds to be credited to a licensed Egyptian bank within 90 days from the bill-of-lading date for goods and within 180 days for services and professional incomes. The mandatory 100% surrender/forced conversion rule was abolished after the 2024 float; exporters may retain proceeds in foreign currency, but any conversion must be executed through a CBE-licensed dealing bank and reported, and non-repatriation requires a CBE exemption.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account – segregated multi-currency settlement and card sponsor bank account (EGP/USD)
Capital Escrow Account and correspondent-backed treasury account (EGP/USD)
Operational Account – global treasury, intercompany liquidity and cross-border clearing hub
Capital Escrow Account and EGP operating account for statutory reserves and payroll
Secondary Operational Account and commercial letter-of-credit facilitation

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for direct operation: foreign EMI or e-money licenses (e.g., FCA or EU-regulated EMIs) confer no passporting or clearing rights in Egypt, and any card issuance, wallet, or payment service activity must be performed by a CBE-licensed payment institution or a licensed bank sponsor under Law No. 18 of 2019. Offshore digital EMIs may serve only as software, processing, or third-party vendor support; fund transfers between the Egyptian LLC and such EMIs are lawful but attract enhanced due diligence and cannot access domestic payment rails without an onshore CBE-licensed settlement counterparty.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for at least one managing director, signatory, or a duly appointed attorney-in-fact holding a notarised and apostilled power of attorney, who must attend an in-person identity interview at a CBE-licensed bank branch in Egypt. Remote or video-KYC is available under CBE e-KYC rules only for natural-person retail accounts and is not extended to High-Risk Special License fintech corporates. All foreign corporate documents require apostille certification, pursuant to Egypt's accession to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention in force as of April 2024, together with a certified Arabic translation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk business classification – virtual card issuing and funds transmission under a non-bank special license
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid CBE Payment Institution license or bank sponsorship agreement; detailed product and transaction-flow architecture; AML/CFT policy aligned with Law No. 80 of 2022 and CBE regulations; appointment of an Egypt-based AML compliance officer; real-time transaction monitoring and sanctions-screening evidence; Travel Rule and card scheme compliance documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership and cross-border control of the Egyptian LLC
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed Ultimate Beneficial Ownership register identifying individuals holding 25% or control; notarised and apostilled certificates of incorporation and corporate standing of the foreign parent; board resolutions approving account opening and authorised signatories; certified Arabic translations; audited financial statements of the ultimate parent; CRS/FATCA status declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity for initial capital escrow and virtual card funding flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of the shareholder from inception or for the prior three years; bank statement of the funding account evidencing the beneficial source; signed declaration of source of wealth; tax clearance certificate where applicable; card scheme settlement files and reconciliation reports evidencing legitimate programmed spend.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Correspondent banking and card scheme settlement concerns (Visa/Mastercard)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Direct card scheme license or sponsored membership through the licensed sponsor bank; acknowledgment letters from principal card associations; Personal Data Protection Law No. 151 of 2020 compliance evidence; segregated client-funds accounting without commingling; restricted-jurisdiction and geoblocking controls; transaction velocity limits and enhanced due diligence on cardholders and merchants.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing requires opening a temporary or post-incorporation capital escrow account with a CBE-licensed bank, with the LLC's incorporation and GAFI registration evidenced to the bank. The shareholder effects an SWIFT MT103 wire classified under the CBE transaction code for direct investment/equity capital inflow; the receiving bank credits the escrow account, issues a Certificate of Inward Transfer for GAFI and CBE verification, and files the inflow under the CBE international transaction reporting rules. Funds may remain in the multi-currency operational account without forced conversion upon presentation of the licensing approval and audited capital utilisation plan.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Onshore EGP payments clear via the CBE RTGS system and the Domestic Instant Payments Network for low-value credits; cross-border disbursements use SWIFT MT103 for direct beneficiary payments, MT202 for bank-to-bank and nostro transfers, and commercial letters of credit (confirmed or unconfirmed) for imports of hardware and POS equipment. Card scheme settlement for the virtual card programme must be executed in USD through the sponsor bank under the Local Currency Settlement Agreement, converting EGP at the market dealing rate, with scheme settlement files and reconciliation statements retained for CBE audit; non-resident merchant payouts are effected as MT103 service/business-income wires accompanied by underlying invoices and CBE documentary support.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable onshore EGP/USD forward contracts, up to 360 days, executed with CBE-licensed dealing banks against bona fide underlying trade, settlement, or capital flows
FX swaps and rollover swaps (USD/EGP) with the relationship bank, settled through RTGS netting to align card-scheme settlement and clearing mismatches
Cross-currency interest-rate and principal swaps (USD/EGP) concluded onshore with licensed banks for long-dated treasury or funding positions

OTC plain-vanilla FX options, collars, and participating forwards executed with an onshore licensed bank under a CBE-compliant derivatives framework; onshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) require a documented underlying exposure and are generally disfavoured post-float

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Department, General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), Egypt
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the calendar month corresponding to the original commercial registration anniversary; registration lapses upon expiry if not renewed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-renewal fine under Law No. 135/1991 (approximately EGP 500-2,000); restriction on notarizing quota transfers and executing contracts; long non-renewal leads to administrative cancellation (strike-off) of the commercial registration after statutory notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return accompanied by Audited Financial Statements and GAFI annual filing of financial statements and partner list
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Income Tax Center / Large Taxpayer Office; GAFI Company and Foreign Investment Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four (4) months after the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, on or before 30 April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 2% per month on unpaid tax (Unified Tax Law No. 7/2025); failure-to-file fines of EGP 2,000-10,000; GAFI company-file flagging and enforced tax assessment when the return is omitted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements and Statutory Compliance Return to the Central Bank of Egypt (card-issuing payment institution)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) - Payment Systems and Financial Technology Supervision Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the financial year-end (by 31 March where the fiscal year ends 31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CBE supervisory penalties under Law No. 18/2019 and Law No. 194/2020; suspension of the corporate virtual-card issuance program; remedial directives; sanctions against responsible licensed managers; and revocation of the CBE license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO / Shareholder Register Confirmation and AML client re-KYC completion certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) through CBE; GAFI Commercial Registry files
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for the AML re-KYC / UBO refresh; within 30 days of any quota transfer or change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML Law No. 80/2002 sanctions with fines up to EGP 500,000 and personal liability of managers; unregistered quota transfers are ineffective against third parties; CBE may refuse license renewal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CBE Regulated Payment / Card-Issuance License - Annual Renewal and Program Authorization Continuation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) - Licensing and Supervision Directorate (Fintech / Regulated Payment Activities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in advance of the license anniversary date; renewal application and supporting compliance documents submitted no later than 60 days before expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to renew halts issuance of virtual corporate cards and terminates Mastercard/Visa network sponsorship; CBE administrative suspension, monetary penalties, and license revocation; mandatory orderly wind-down of outstanding card programs.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday or sector-specific corporate income tax incentive applies to a standalone Egyptian LLC operating as a virtual corporate card issuer. Preferential deductions are limited to ordinary business costs, bad-debt provisions compliant with Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) prudential rules, and the five-year tax-loss carryforward under Income Tax Law 91/2005.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return, Model No. 198, filed exclusively through the Egyptian Tax Authority electronic filing portal (e-taxation.gov.eg).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filed within four months after the end of the corporate tax year. For calendar-year filers, the return and final CIT payment are due on or before 30 April of the immediately following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identity fields: taxpayer ID, commercial register number, tax card number, legal form, address, authorised signatory, and board composition.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not file this section. The Egyptian LLC enters its own statutory details only; foreign ownership percentages are disclosed in the accompanying equity schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from card scheme interchange, gross load fees, virtual card issuance fees, B2B spend management platform fees, merchant rebates, and foreign exchange spreads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all revenue derived through an Egyptian permanent establishment, including fees sourced from overseas clients where the underlying card-issuing activity is managed from Egypt. Foreign-sourced revenue attributable to the Egyptian LLC is included at arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: Mastercard and Visa network assessments, processing and gateway costs, chargeback reserves, IT infrastructure, office rent, salaries, professional fees, depreciation, and CBE supervisory levies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party charges must be supported by a transfer-pricing documentation file and disclosed under Article 57. Payments to foreign affiliates for software or management services require a withholding-tax clearance certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of net taxable profit or loss after statutory adjustments, including disallowed provisions, excess depreciation, and loss carryforward utilisation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not mix non-resident shareholder-level losses with LLC losses. Losses incurred by offshore group entities are not offsettable against Egyptian taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit and double taxation treaty relief schedule, including taxes withheld on foreign interest, royalties, or technical service income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A certified Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and the ETA international-tax approval letter must be attached to claim reduced treaty withholding rates. No unilateral foreign tax credit is available for taxes attributable to wholly foreign activities unrelated to Egypt.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a fixed penalty of EGP 500 to EGP 2,000 per return plus a monthly surcharge of 2% of the outstanding CIT balance until full settlement. Where false or misleading statements lead to under-assessed tax, an additional penalty of 50% of the tax difference is imposed, with criminal prosecution under Law 91/2005 if fraudulent intent is proven.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends distributed to non-resident corporate shareholders. No withholding applies to profits retained in the LLC; a distribution resolved by the general meeting triggers the obligation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply the lower treaty rate, the LLC must submit to the ETA International Taxation Department: a completed DTA relief application form, a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign shareholder's competent authority, a beneficial-ownership declaration, board minutes approving the distribution, and an explanation of the applicable treaty article. ETA clearance should be requested before remitting the dividend; if clearance is received after the withholding, the excess WHT is recoverable by refund or set-off in the next annual CIT settlement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory source withholding is 20% for interest and 20% for royalties paid to non-residents. Most Egyptian double tax treaties reduce royalty and/or interest rates to 10%–15%, conditioned on a valid TRC, beneficial ownership, and the absence of a permanent establishment in Egypt.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 1,000,000 cumulative related-party transactions in the tax year triggers mandatory Local File preparation. Master File compliance is required where the multinational group's consolidated turnover exceeds EGP 2,000,000,000. A related-party disclosure schedule must be attached to the CIT return in all cases where controlled transactions occur.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not yet apply a full standalone Economic Substance Regulations cascade, but the ETA and CBE apply an equivalent substance doctrine when assessing residency, treaty entitlement, and the validity of cross-border cost allocations. The Egyptian LLC must demonstrate an actual head office in Egypt, substantive employment contracts, local board decision-making, locally controlled card-platform systems, and capital deployed at risk. A letter-box company routed through Egyptian incorporation for tax advantage will be denied treaty relief, have its deductibility challenged, and may be recommended for de-registration by CBE.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-declaring revenue generated by virtual card interchange fees, transaction loads, and B2B spend management commissions; inflating chargeback expenses without documentary proof; shifting Egyptian revenue to a dormant overseas subsidiary through artificial management fees without transfer-pricing analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Income Tax Law 91/2005 and Tax Procedures Law 23/2016, the law imposes a fine of up to EGP 1,000,000 in addition to the evaded tax, an evasion surcharge of 50% of the tax difference, confiscation of records and assets used in the evasion, and imprisonment for responsible officers for up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns or knowingly participate in the evasion are jointly and severally liable for the LLC's unpaid CIT, and the corporate veil will be pierced to recover assets from personal bank accounts. ETA may issue a travel ban, freeze personal assets, and enter a director disqualification order of up to ten years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the virtual card issuing business through a nominal Egyptian LLC with no real employees, no local office, no physical or logical servers in Egypt, no independent management meetings, and no local compliance function; all profit immediately routed to offshore principals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA may deny resident status and treaty benefits, disallow the arrangement as sham, reattribute the Egyptian card-issuing income to the actual beneficial owners, and assess CIT at 22.5% on the deemed taxable amount together with a 2% monthly delay surcharge. CBE may revoke any relevant payment-service approvals and request judicial winding-up of the entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors acting as authorised signatories on behalf of a façade company face civil recovery of all remaining CIT and penalties; criminal liability may arise for aiding a sham arrangement, and the courts may impose travel bans and asset freezes pending final determination.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / CFT Non-Compliance in Virtual Card Issuance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to perform customer due diligence on corporate cardholders, allowing reloadable virtual cards to be funded from unverified sources, disregarding negative media and sanctioned-entity screening, failing to implement transaction monitoring, and omitting to file suspicious transaction reports with the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 80/2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended, imposes imprisonment of three to ten years, fines of EGP 100,000 to EGP 2,000,000, confiscation of the touched funds and card infrastructure, and mandatory licence revocation by CBE. Banks and Mastercard/Visa member institutions may also levy contractual penalties of up to the full value of the undertaking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML compliance officers, nominated directors, and board members who are proven to have engaged in willful blindness are personally and criminally liable; CBE may issue a personal banking ban, freeze their assets, and prohibit them from holding any role in a financial institution for a remediable period not exceeding 15 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing virtual corporate cards to end clients without a valid CBE payment-service authorisation or without Mastercard/Visa programme sponsorship; operating under the false characterisation of a technology company when the business constitutes card issuance, load, and settlement services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Banking Law No. 194/2020 and CBE implementing directives classify unlicensed card issuing as a banking offence. Sanctions include imprisonment up to ten years, fines from EGP 100,000 to EGP 2,000,000, confiscation of all funds and processing equipment, court-ordered liquidation of the LLC, and prohibition of the entity from reapplying for any Egyptian financial licence for ten years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil will be pierced where the LLC was used to disguise unlicensed banking. Directors and senior executives face personal liability for all client losses, CBE disciplinary orders banning them from banking and financial services, and in aggravated cases, preventive detention pending investigation and travel bans enforced by the public prosecutor.
